text:
sanjay: heads up — seeing a cluster of GPU launches stuck in PENDING in eu-west3, several failures citing local storage errors
maya: ack, seeing a bunch of failed pods with 'mount failed: I/O error' on /scratch
lee: ops-bot alert just triggered: gnode-121 queue_depth at 95% -> io wait skyrocketed :warning:
ops-bot: [ALERT] gnode-121 nvme_iops_saturated (5m avg) - count=24 pods impacted, metric=nvme:qdepth
jorge: iostat on gnode-121: 
```
avg-cpu:  %user   %nice %system %iowait  %steal   %idle
           3.2    0.0    6.1    88.9    0.0    1.8
Device            tps    kB_read/s    kB_wrtn/s    kB_read    kB_wrtn
nvme0n1         1800      1024         512        61440     30720
```
lee: that iowait number is wild. background janitor scrub started at 03:00 UTC for the pool?
maya: scrub cron shows overlap: scrub-job and ephemeral-cleaner both ran on the same shard window, probably contention + wear-leveling GC
sanjay: timeline: scrub kicked off -> immediate qdepth rise -> scheduler couldn't allocate GPUs because local disk probe timed out -> pod stuck pending
nina: quick mitigation options: 1) pause scrub on affected nodes 2) drain affected nodes 3) throttle cleaner concurrency
jorge: can we throttle cleaner? disk-cleaner-bot supports concurrency override: `cleaner set-concurrency --pool scratch-eu-west3 --concurrency 2`
disk-cleaner-bot: command accepted. Pool scratch-eu-west3 concurrency set to 2 by jorge
lee: I'm going to cordon+drain gnode-121 to unblock provisioning, will migrate running workloads to us-west2 as a fallback
maya: before draining, let's set scheduling soft-affinity for batch jobs so they can move off nodes with disk pressure. Also temporarily lower per-request batch size from 1024 to 512 to reduce IO bursts
sanjay: cost note — if this keeps recurring we need to decide: 1) increase overprovisioning (lower usable capacity) 2) replace with higher-end endurance drives (warranty claim + CapEx) 3) change janitor cadence. Replacements hit budget but reduce risk to SLAs
nina: can we run a wear-map pass to identify hot drives? If it's firmware-level trashing we should involve vendor. I'll open HW ticket with SMART logs attached
jorge: grabbing SMART + dmesg now, dropping into #incidents if we need paging
ops-bot: [INFO] scheduled mitigations: cordon gnode-121, reduce cleaner concurrency, escalated to storage@vendor for investigation
lee: cordon/evict started, ETA ~7m to finish. Prefers rolling drains to avoid mass scheduling thrash
sanjay: once drained, let's run fio quick pattern test with `--iodepth=32 --bs=64k` to validate latency tail after eviction
maya: agreed. After that, revert scheduler rules and monitor tokenized launch success rate for 30m before full resume
jorge: attaching short logs to the thread:
```
[2026-03-20T10:12:34Z] kubelet: mount failed: I/O error
[2026-03-20T10:12:40Z] nvme: qdepth spike -> 1042
[2026-03-20T10:14:01Z] janitor: scrub-start pool=scratch-eu-west3 shard=7
```
nina: opened vendor ticket #ST-4721 with SMART dumps and iostat; requested priority review and potential RMA
sanjay: thanks — keep this thread updated. If vendor confirms firmware-induced GC we might need a fleet-wide staggered scrub schedule to avoid synchronized I/O storms
maya: adding postmortem owners: sanjay, lee, nina. Will draft incident note after stabilization :memo:
lee: nodes draining complete, new GPU allocations proceeding, watch for residual failures and I'll keep drains slower if we see requeue thrash
jorge: monitoring dashboard: nvme qdepth trending down after concurrency change, jobs slowly requeue and launch
sanjay: good progress. after stable window, propose changing scrub windows to randomized offsets and add a safety check in janitor to abort if node qdepth > 80%
maya: agreed. I'll create a PR for janitor safety gate and schedule randomized offsets for eu-west3, target rollout tomorrow low-traffic window :shipit:
ops-bot: [RESOLVED] immediate provisioning impact mitigated. Continue to monitor for 2h.
